description: Deep level ratio (bid_size_3..5 vs ask_size_3..5) computed from 15-30s window after market open instead of first 5s. Hypothesis: MMs need time to react to opening price, so delayed snapshot captures informed positioning rather than stale pre-positioned orders.
hypothesis: Deep level ratio from 15-30s window produces stronger directional signal than 0-5s window because MMs have had time to observe the opening mid-price and adjust their deep levels accordingly.
next_steps: Hypothesis refuted: the delayed 15-30s window (51.5% WR, $0.28/trade, Sharpe 0.50) is strictly WEAKER than the early 0-5s window (55.7% WR, $0.52/trade, Sharpe 0.90). Deep ratio variance compresses from 0.14 to 0.085 as MMs converge toward fair value, diluting the signal. The initial 'stale' orders in the 0-5s window actually carry MORE information — they likely reflect pre-positioned informed views, not noise. The early deep level ratio signal itself is interesting (Sharpe ~0.9 on 2,872 markets) but needs walk-forward validation before trusting.
